macro.description: Define a reusable template function that can accept arguments and return rendered output.
macro.caveat: Macros perform no type checking. Variables defined inside a macro are local. Recursive macros may cause stack overflows.

if.syntax: {% if condition %}...{% elif condition %}...{% else %}...{% endif %}
if.description: Conditionally render blocks based on the truth value of expressions.
if.caveat: Conditions follow Python truthiness rules: empty sequences, empty strings, None, and 0 evaluate to False.

set.syntax: {% set name = value %} | {% set name %}...{% endset %}
set.description: Assign a value to a variable within the template. Supports both single-line assignment and block assignment.
set.caveat: Assignments are scoped to the current context. Block assignments capture rendered text, not expressions.

for.syntax: {% for target in iterable %}...{% else %}...{% endfor %}
for.description: Iterate over an iterable (such as a list, tuple, or dict) and render the block for each item.
for.caveat: Loop variables are only available inside the loop body.

do.description: Evaluate an expression for its side effects without rendering its result.
do.caveat: The result is discarded. To display a value, use {{ }} instead.

selectattr.caveat: Objects without the attribute are skipped.

list.description: Convert a value into a list.
list.caveat: Strings are split into individual characters.

trim.description: Strip characters from both ends of a string.

join.description: Join items into a string using a delimiter.

length.description: Return the number of items in an object.
length.caveat: Returns 0 for objects without a defined length.

unique.description: Return unique items from a sequence while preserving order.
unique.caveat: Returns an iterator; convert to list if reuse is needed.

sort.caveat: Elements must be comparable; attribute must exist on objects.
